hardware.gpu: NVIDIA RTX 5000 Ada Generation Laptop GPU
hardware.note: WSL memory is shared by its distributions. Swap occupied alone was not treated as proof of current paging; vmstat also observed active page-in.

conclusions: 30B reported 22090505198 bytes total and 14605027900 bytes in VRAM; 14B reported 14383820307 bytes total, all in VRAM.
Observed first-call model load: 74.3 seconds for 30B and 11.4 seconds for 14B. OS page cache and service load were not controlled.
Observed generation rate: 19.35–25.03 tokens/s for 30B and 28.99–31.33 for 14B; tiny outputs do not establish full-task latency.
Both edited the synthetic line correctly. 30B falsely claimed a missing confirmation present in the supplied sibling module; 14B did not.
This sample cannot select a production winner or prove success on the jewelry catalog.

recommendations.action: Qualify a smaller fully GPU-resident model on representative tasks, including healthy-code negative controls; candidates Qwen3.5 9B and Gemma4 12B, not yet installed or tested.
Replace large one-shot patch production with a bounded read/edit/validate loop in an isolated workspace pinned to the authorized SHA; retain permissions, audits, MR, review and security gates.
Use task-specific context and output budgets, never silent truncation; measure Flash Attention and q8_0 KV cache before adoption.
Create a deliberate lightweight service profile; do not stop user services or raise WSL RAM merely to shift pressure to Windows.
For heavier coding models, prefer a separate private inference machine. Initial engineering target: 64 GB host RAM and 32 GB GPU VRAM; validate the chosen model/context before purchasing hardware.
